options.a: Conventional LTV is high (commonly above 80%)
options.b: An FHA loan is used with a down payment of 3.5%
options.c: A VA loan is used with no down payment at all
options.d: Conventional LTV falls to 78% of original value

distractorExplanations.b: FHA loans carry the government's mortgage insurance premium (MIP), not private mortgage insurance.
distractorExplanations.c: VA loans are guaranteed by the VA and do not require PMI even with no down payment; a funding fee applies instead.
distractorExplanations.d: 78% of original value is when borrower-paid PMI terminates under the Homeowners Protection Act, not when it starts.

options.a: Upon the death of the remainderman
options.b: When the life tenant sells the estate
options.c: Upon the death of the original grantor
options.d: Upon the death of the measuring life

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses the remainderman with the measuring life; if the remainderman dies first, the remainder passes to his heirs and the life estate continues.
distractorExplanations.b: A life tenant may convey the interest, but the buyer simply holds a life estate pur autre vie that still ends at the original tenant's death.
distractorExplanations.c: Confuses the grantor with the measuring life; the grantor's death does not end an estate measured by the life tenant's life.

oh-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Life estates are measured by a life; the estate ends when the measuring life dies (or as otherwise defined in the grant), and the remainder or reversion follows.

options.a: Obtain the highest price by carrying out every seller instruction, lawful or not
options.b: Owe the buyer customer the same loyalty and confidentiality as the seller
options.c: Promote the seller's interests with loyalty, care, and obedience within the law
options.d: Guarantee the seller a closed sale at list price within the listing term

distractorExplanations.a: Obedience extends only to lawful instructions; a broker must refuse illegal directions such as discriminatory or fraudulent ones.
distractorExplanations.b: Confuses client and customer: a buyer customer is owed honesty and fair dealing, not the fiduciary loyalty owed to the seller client.
distractorExplanations.d: Fiduciary duties concern conduct (loyalty, care, obedience), not guaranteed outcomes; brokers cannot promise a sale or price.

options.a: The broker's compensation is a fixed percentage of the final sale price
options.b: The broker's compensation is the amount above a seller's net price
options.c: The seller keeps the right to sell on their own without owing a commission
options.d: The broker's flat fee is owed up front even if the property does not sell

distractorExplanations.a: That describes a standard percentage commission listing, which does not create the net listing's incentive to underprice.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes an exclusive agency listing, not a net listing where the broker keeps everything above the seller's net.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses a net listing with a flat-fee or advance-fee arrangement; a net listing pays the broker only the excess over the net price.

oh-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Net listings pay the broker the amount above the seller's net price, creating conflict-of-interest concerns: they can incentivize underpricing and are banned or tightly regulated in many places.

options.a: Maximum loan-to-value ratios that lenders may offer on certain loans
options.b: Minimum disclosures of APR and finance charges on consumer loans
options.c: Maximum interest rates that may be charged on certain loans
options.d: Maximum property tax rates that local governments may levy

distractorExplanations.a: LTV limits come from lender and investor underwriting guidelines, not usury laws, which cap the interest rate charged.
distractorExplanations.b: That is the Truth in Lending Act (Regulation Z), which requires cost disclosure but does not cap interest rates.
distractorExplanations.d: Property tax limits are set by tax and levy laws; usury laws apply to interest charged by lenders on loans.

options.a: The seller's reason for selling and lowest acceptable price, even if the seller objects
options.b: The racial or religious makeup of the neighborhood, since it may affect desirability
options.c: Known latent defects or conditions that could significantly affect value or desirability
options.d: Obvious patent defects, while hidden latent defects are left for the buyer's own inspection

distractorExplanations.a: Seller motivation and bottom-line price are confidential client information, not material property facts a buyer must be told.
distractorExplanations.b: Commenting on a neighborhood's race or religion is steering under the Fair Housing Act, not a required material-fact disclosure.
distractorExplanations.d: Reverses the rule: known latent (hidden) defects are exactly what must be disclosed, because a buyer cannot readily discover them.

oh-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Material property defects and legally required disclosures must be shared, as required by law; confidential motivations may be protected.

options.a: Interest alone, with the full principal due as a balloon at maturity
options.b: Part of the interest, with the unpaid rest added to the balance
options.c: Interest plus escrowed taxes and insurance, with no principal reduction
options.d: Both interest and principal so the balance declines over the term

distractorExplanations.a: That describes an interest-only or balloon loan; an amortizing payment repays principal with each installment.
distractorExplanations.b: Adding unpaid interest to the balance is negative amortization, the opposite of a fully amortizing payment.
distractorExplanations.c: Escrowed taxes and insurance may be added to PITI, but an amortizing payment still reduces principal every month.

options.a: Banning certain kickbacks and requiring settlement cost disclosures
options.b: Requiring APR and finance charge disclosures for all consumer credit
options.c: Prohibiting lending discrimination based on race, sex, or marital status
options.d: Requiring lenders to report loan data by census tract to regulators

distractorExplanations.b: APR and finance-charge disclosure is the Truth in Lending Act (Regulation Z), not RESPA's settlement-services focus.
distractorExplanations.c: That is the Equal Credit Opportunity Act (ECOA); RESPA targets settlement kickbacks and closing-cost disclosure.
distractorExplanations.d: Census-tract loan reporting is the Home Mortgage Disclosure Act (HMDA), which tracks lending patterns, not settlement costs.

oh-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-a.explanation: RESPA addresses settlement services, kickbacks, and related disclosures in covered transactions (with TRID integration for many loans).

options.a: The listing broker earns a commission during the term except when the seller personally finds the buyer
options.b: The listing broker is owed a commission if the property sells during the term, regardless of who finds the buyer
options.c: Any cooperating broker who is the procuring cause earns the commission, and the seller may list with other firms
options.d: The broker keeps any proceeds above the seller's stated net price as compensation for the sale

distractorExplanations.a: That describes an exclusive agency listing, where the seller keeps the right to sell on their own without owing a commission.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes an open listing, where only the procuring broker is paid and the seller may list with several firms.
distractorExplanations.d: That describes a net listing, which is restricted or banned in many places; it is a compensation method, not exclusive right-to-sell.

oh-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Exclusive right-to-sell typically protects the listing broker's commission if a sale occurs during the listing term (per the agreement).

options.a: Practicing law any time they fill in a standard form's blanks for a client
options.b: Permitted to draft custom clauses as long as the client signs a waiver
options.c: Practicing law if they draft novel legal clauses beyond authorized forms
options.d: Required to have the client's attorney approve each filled-in form first

distractorExplanations.a: Filling in approved standard forms is generally permitted for licensees; drafting new legal language is what crosses into law practice.
distractorExplanations.b: A client waiver does not authorize a licensee to practice law; drafting novel legal clauses remains unauthorized practice.
distractorExplanations.d: Attorney review may be advisable or a contract contingency, but it is not a general prerequisite to completing standard forms.

options.a: Land bordering a still lake, sea, or ocean
options.b: Water use based on first in time, first in right by permit
options.c: Land bordering flowing water such as a river or stream
options.d: Ownership of subsurface minerals beneath a parcel of land

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses riparian with littoral rights, which apply to land bordering lakes, seas, and oceans rather than flowing water.
distractorExplanations.b: That describes the prior appropriation doctrine, a contrasting permit system, not riparian rights tied to bordering land.
distractorExplanations.d: Subsurface rights cover minerals and can be severed; riparian rights concern use of water by land bordering a stream.

options.a: 1% of the purchase price
options.b: 1% of the down payment
options.c: 1% of the loan amount
options.d: 1% of the interest rate

distractorExplanations.a: Points are computed on the loan amount, not the price; on a $200,000 price with a $160,000 loan, one point is $1,600.
distractorExplanations.b: Uses the wrong base: the down payment is the buyer's equity, while points are a percentage of the amount borrowed.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses one point (1% of the loan amount) with one percentage point of interest rate; a point typically buys down far less.

options.a: Originate new loans directly to borrowers at closing
options.b: Insure lenders against borrower default on high-LTV loans
options.c: Buy and sell existing mortgages, improving liquidity
options.d: Set the discount rate that member banks pay the Fed

distractorExplanations.a: That describes the primary mortgage market, where lenders originate loans; the secondary market buys loans already made.
distractorExplanations.b: That is the role of private mortgage insurance or FHA insurance, not the secondary market's buying and selling of loans.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses the secondary market with the Federal Reserve, which sets the discount rate as a monetary-policy tool.

oh-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-a.explanation: Entities like Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac (and others) buy existing loans, improving liquidity for originators so they can lend again.

options.a: An obligation to purchase on stated terms within a period, once consideration is paid
options.b: A right of first refusal to match any offer the owner later accepts
options.c: A right to purchase on stated terms within a period, usually for consideration
options.d: An equitable title that passes legal title once payments are complete

distractorExplanations.a: Only the optionor (owner) is bound; the optionee holds a right, not an obligation, to buy, making the option unilateral.
distractorExplanations.b: A right of first refusal only lets the holder match a third-party offer; an option fixes the price and terms in advance.
distractorExplanations.d: That describes a vendee's position under a land contract (contract for deed), not an optionee's unexercised right.

options.a: A zoning variance granted to the owner for a hardship use
options.b: A deed recorded with a full covenant of warranty from the grantor
options.c: A claim, encumbrance, or defect that may impair marketability
options.d: The abstract summary of the chain of title prepared for a buyer

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses public land-use control with title: a variance governs permitted use and is not a claim against ownership.
distractorExplanations.b: A recorded general warranty deed strengthens the chain of title; it is the opposite of a cloud that casts doubt on it.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses an abstract of title (a history of recorded documents) with a cloud, which is a defect or claim the abstract may reveal.

options.a: Before or as soon as practicable when the dual/designated relationship arises
options.b: At closing, when the broker's compensation appears on the Closing Disclosure
options.c: Only after an offer is accepted and both parties have signed the contract
options.d: After the inspection period ends, once the buyer is committed to the purchase

distractorExplanations.b: Closing is far too late; informed consent to dual or designated agency must come before the parties rely on it.
distractorExplanations.c: Waiting until after acceptance denies the parties informed consent during negotiations, when the conflict matters most.
distractorExplanations.d: Disclosure tied to a later contract milestone is too late; it is required when the dual relationship first arises.

oh-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Agency disclosure timing is early—when the dual or designated relationship is created or contemplated, per applicable rules.

options.a: Refuse to share any property facts until the buyer hires a buyer agent
options.b: Recommend an offer amount, since customers are owed the same advice as clients
options.c: Avoid acting as the buyer's advocate and stay within the listing agency role
options.d: Share the seller's lowest acceptable price so the buyer can make a fair offer

distractorExplanations.a: Listing agents owe customers honesty and may share property facts; the limit is on advocacy, not on providing information.
distractorExplanations.b: Confuses customer and client: advising a buyer on price is advocacy that conflicts with the agent's loyalty to the seller.
distractorExplanations.d: Revealing the seller's bottom line breaches the confidentiality the listing agent owes to the seller client.

oh-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Listing agents represent the seller; advocacy for a buyer requires a proper agency shift and disclosure (or properly creating buyer agency if allowed).

options.a: Parties may still perform within a reasonable time after each stated deadline passes
options.b: The closing date is firm, but other contingency deadlines may slip
options.c: Contract dates and times are critical and late performance may be a breach
options.d: The offer expires if the seller does not accept it within 24 hours

distractorExplanations.a: That is the default rule when the clause is absent; time is of the essence makes the stated deadlines strictly enforceable.
distractorExplanations.b: The clause applies to all contract dates, including inspection, financing, and appraisal contingency deadlines.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses the clause with an offer's expiration term; time is of the essence governs performance deadlines in the contract.

options.a: Proceed with dual agency once the buyer consents in writing, since one party's consent suffices
options.b: Not create the dual agency relationship; consider designated agency, referral, or withdrawal
options.c: Act as a dual agent for both parties but keep each side's confidential information private
options.d: Represent the buyer and treat the seller as a customer while keeping the listing

distractorExplanations.a: Dual agency requires informed consent from both clients; the buyer's consent alone cannot override the seller's refusal.
distractorExplanations.c: Keeping confidences does not replace consent; without the seller's agreement the broker may not act as a dual agent.
distractorExplanations.d: The broker cannot downgrade an existing seller client to customer status to sidestep the required dual agency consent.

oh-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Consent is required for dual agency where the model is used; without it, other compliant paths are needed (designated agency, referral, or withdrawal as appropriate).

options.a: Use allowed in a district only after a special permit is issued
options.b: Lawful use that predates current zoning and may continue as is
options.c: Permission to deviate from a zoning requirement due to hardship
options.d: Permanent change of the zoning map for an entire district

distractorExplanations.a: That describes a conditional or special use permit, which allows a listed use under conditions rather than relief for hardship.
distractorExplanations.b: That describes a nonconforming use (grandfathered use), which predates the ordinance rather than being granted relief from it.
distractorExplanations.d: That is rezoning/amendment.

oh-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Variances grant relief from strict zoning application in hardship cases, granted by the zoning authority (such as a board of zoning appeals).

options.a: Signed under a mistaken belief about the market value
options.b: Was induced by fraud or was a minor
options.c: Later found a better-priced property elsewhere
options.d: Changed their mind before closing

distractorExplanations.a: A one-sided mistake about value or a bad bargain does not make a contract voidable; fraud or incapacity does.
distractorExplanations.c: Buyer's remorse over a better deal is not a legal ground to void a contract; that would be a breach.
distractorExplanations.d: Changing one's mind after a binding contract is formed is a breach, not a ground that makes the contract voidable.

oh-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Fraud or lack of capacity can make a contract voidable by the protected party. Whether a particular contract is voidable depends on the circumstances and state law.

options.a: A misstatement of a measurable fact, such as lot size, that buyers may rely upon
options.b: An implied warranty of quality that binds the seller once the buyer relies on it
options.c: Exaggerated opinion that a reasonable person would not treat as a factual warranty
options.d: A form of negligent misrepresentation that licensees are liable for if a buyer relies on it

distractorExplanations.a: That is misrepresentation; puffing is vague opinion, while measurable facts like lot size must be accurate.
distractorExplanations.b: Puffing creates no warranty; a reasonable buyer is not expected to treat sales talk as a promise of quality.
distractorExplanations.d: Negligent misrepresentation involves a false statement of fact; opinion-level puffing is not actionable on its own.

options.a: Spending client trust money on the broker's own business expenses
options.b: Holding earnest money for several different clients in one pooled trust account
options.c: Depositing earnest money after the legally required deadline
options.d: Mixing client trust money with personal or operating funds improperly

distractorExplanations.a: That is conversion (using trust money for oneself); commingling is the mixing of funds, even if none is spent.
distractorExplanations.b: A pooled trust account for multiple clients with proper ledgers is permitted; commingling is mixing trust and broker money.
distractorExplanations.c: A late deposit violates the deposit timeline rule, not the commingling rule against mixing trust and personal funds.

options.a: Devise by will
options.b: Survivorship
options.c: Homestead
options.d: Curtesy

distractorExplanations.a: A joint tenant cannot pass the interest by will; survivorship gives it to the surviving co-owners.
distractorExplanations.c: Homestead is a separate protection for a primary residence, not a defining feature of joint tenancy.
distractorExplanations.d: Curtesy is a husband's marital life interest (largely abolished), not a feature of joint tenancy.

options.a: Public use and the owner's written consent
options.b: Just compensation equal to the assessed value
options.c: Police power and a zoning hearing
options.d: Public use/purpose and just compensation

distractorExplanations.a: Eminent domain is a forced taking; the owner's consent is not required, only public use and just compensation.
distractorExplanations.b: Just compensation is measured by fair market value, not the tax-assessed value, and public use is also required.
distractorExplanations.c: Confuses eminent domain with police power regulation, which restricts use without taking title or paying compensation.

oh-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Takings require public purpose and just compensation under the Constitution. This is the Fifth Amendment takings framework.

options.a: May hold unequal shares and typically lack survivorship
options.b: Must acquire title at the same time and by the same deed
options.c: Hold equal shares but may sell only with the others' consent
options.d: Have survivorship rights but may not devise their shares by will

distractorExplanations.b: Unities of time and title are required for joint tenancy; tenants in common need only unity of possession.
distractorExplanations.c: Tenants in common may hold unequal shares and may convey their interests without the others' consent.
distractorExplanations.d: Reverses the rule: tenants in common can devise their shares by will and have no automatic survivorship.

oh-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: TIC allows unequal interests and no automatic survivorship. Survivorship applies only if the deed specifies it.

options.a: Delivering the signed deed to the grantee
options.b: Having the grantor's signature notarized
options.c: Recording the deed in the public land records
options.d: Taking open physical possession of the land

distractorExplanations.a: Delivery and acceptance transfer title between the parties but give no notice to the world; recording does.
distractorExplanations.b: Acknowledgment (notarization) usually makes a deed eligible for recording but does not itself give constructive notice.
distractorExplanations.d: Possession gives inquiry (actual) notice to those who inspect, not the constructive notice created by recording.

options.a: Lets the lender call the full balance due if the property is sold
options.b: Adds a late charge when a payment arrives after the grace period
options.c: Charges a fee to assume the existing loan
options.d: Requires extra payment if the borrower pays off early

distractorExplanations.a: Describes a due-on-sale (alienation) clause, which is triggered by transfer, not by early payoff.
distractorExplanations.b: That is a late-payment charge for paying too late, the opposite of a penalty for paying off early.
distractorExplanations.c: An assumption fee applies when a buyer takes over the loan; a prepayment penalty applies to early payoff.

oh-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-a.explanation: Prepayment penalties charge for early payoff when permitted by the loan terms and law. It applies only when the note and applicable law allow it.

options.a: Can adjust based on an index plus margin, subject to caps
options.b: Adjusts by the margin alone, with the index fixed at closing
options.c: Adjusts to the current prime rate with no periodic caps
options.d: Changes only when the borrower elects to refinance

distractorExplanations.b: The margin is the fixed part; the index moves with the market and drives each adjustment.
distractorExplanations.c: ARMs follow the index named in the note, not necessarily prime, and most carry periodic and lifetime caps.
distractorExplanations.d: An ARM rate resets on its schedule without a refinance; refinancing replaces the loan entirely.

options.a: Borrower default on the loan, protecting the lender's unpaid balance
options.b: Covered title defects and claims against ownership per the policy
options.c: Physical damage to the home from fire or storm
options.d: Construction defects discovered after the buyer closes

distractorExplanations.a: Default protection is private mortgage insurance (PMI) or FHA insurance, not title insurance.
distractorExplanations.c: Casualty damage is covered by hazard (homeowner's) insurance; title insurance covers ownership defects.
distractorExplanations.d: Physical construction defects fall under warranties or disclosure claims, not a title policy's coverage of ownership defects.

options.a: The buyer is credited; it reduces the cash needed
options.b: The seller is charged the item on the buyer's behalf
options.c: The lender pays the item at closing
options.d: The buyer is charged; it increases cash needed

distractorExplanations.a: Reverses the entry: a credit reduces the buyer's cash to close, while a debit is a charge that increases it.
distractorExplanations.b: A buyer debit charges the buyer; a seller-paid item would appear as a seller debit and buyer credit.
distractorExplanations.c: Lender-paid items show as credits to the buyer; a buyer debit means the buyer pays.

oh-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-a.explanation: Debits charge a party; buyer debits typically increase funds due at closing. For the seller, a debit reduces sale proceeds.

options.a: Finance a short-term gap, often between purchase of a new home and sale of an existing one
options.b: Fund construction draws on a new home and then convert to permanent financing once it is completed
options.c: Let a buyer take over the seller's existing loan at its current rate and terms
options.d: Combine a first mortgage with a second loan to avoid PMI on a low down payment

distractorExplanations.b: Describes a construction-to-permanent loan, not a short-term bridge between buying and selling homes.
distractorExplanations.c: Describes a loan assumption, which transfers an existing mortgage rather than covering a short timing gap.
distractorExplanations.d: Describes a piggyback (80/10/10) loan structure used to avoid PMI, not a bridge loan.

options.a: Restricted under federal RESPA rules
options.b: Permitted when the fee is disclosed to the borrower in writing
options.c: Permitted between affiliated businesses without any disclosure
options.d: Legal if paid by the lender

distractorExplanations.b: Disclosure does not cure a RESPA Section 8 kickback; fees for referrals alone are prohibited.
distractorExplanations.c: Affiliated business arrangements are allowed only with the required written disclosure and no referral-fee payment.
distractorExplanations.d: RESPA's ban covers referral fees from any settlement provider, including lenders.

oh-real-estate-readiness-check-oh-licens.explanation: RESPA bans certain referral fees; state ethics/license rules also police improper inducements. Improper referral fees may also violate state license law and standards of practice.

options.a: Follow lawful client instructions and brokerage policy for timely presentation/notification
options.b: Hold the offer until a second offer arrives so that both offers can be presented together
options.c: Ask the buyer's agent to resubmit the offer once the seller can be reached
options.d: Have the principal broker accept the offer under the listing agreement's authority

distractorExplanations.b: Offers must be presented promptly as received; holding one back to batch offers breaches the duty to present.
distractorExplanations.c: The listing agent must handle the offer it already received; asking for a resubmission delays presentation.
distractorExplanations.d: A listing agreement does not give the principal broker authority to accept offers; only the seller can accept.

oh-real-estate-readiness-check-oh-licens.explanation: Offers must be handled per agency duties and any written seller instructions. An offer is never ignored.

options.a: May negotiate offer terms if the supervising broker reviews and approves them afterward
options.b: May show property and discuss price unsupervised once trained by the firm
options.c: Performs administrative tasks under supervision and must not negotiate unless licensed
options.d: Performs licensed tasks under a broker's supervision without needing a license

distractorExplanations.a: Negotiating is licensed activity; after-the-fact broker approval does not let an unlicensed coordinator negotiate.
distractorExplanations.b: Showing property and discussing price are licensed activities; firm training does not replace a license.
distractorExplanations.d: Supervision does not authorize unlicensed people to perform licensed activities; only clerical tasks are allowed.

options.a: Immediately investigate, correct, and report/notify as required
options.b: Wait for the next monthly reconciliation to confirm the shortage
options.c: Report it if a client files a complaint about missing funds
options.d: Close the trust account and open a new one at another bank

distractorExplanations.b: Delaying until the next reconciliation leaves client funds short; a known shortage must be investigated and cured now.
distractorExplanations.c: Reporting duties do not depend on a client complaint; the broker must act and notify when the shortage is found.
distractorExplanations.d: Moving banks does not cure the shortage and may hide it; the deficit must be corrected and reported.

oh-real-estate-readiness-check-oh-licens.explanation: Shortages are serious; prompt remediation and required notices protect the public. Reporting and notice duties follow the state commission's trust account rules.

options.a: As brokerage income once the transaction closes, without any written disclosure to the parties
options.b: According to statutory rules (e.g., client benefit or approved housing-trust programs)
options.c: By splitting it between the listing and selling brokers at closing
options.d: By paying it to the state real estate recovery fund in every case

distractorExplanations.a: Interest on trust money is not the broker's to keep without authority; keeping it undisclosed is conversion.
distractorExplanations.c: Cooperating brokers have no claim to trust-account interest; its use is set by statute or the parties' agreement.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses trust interest with recovery-fund fees; interest goes where statute or the agreement directs, such as the client.

options.a: Documents supervision standards and compliant procedures for affiliated licensees
options.b: Shifts liability for agents' violations from the broker to the agents
options.c: Takes the place of required continuing education for affiliated licensees
options.d: Satisfies the broker's supervision duty without any further review of agents' files

distractorExplanations.b: A manual does not transfer the broker's supervisory liability; the broker remains responsible for supervision.
distractorExplanations.c: Continuing education is a separate licensing requirement that a policy manual cannot replace.
distractorExplanations.d: A written manual supports but does not satisfy supervision; brokers must still actively review transactions.

options.a: Pay the rebate directly from the earnest money deposit at closing
options.b: Refuse, because federal RESPA bans all commission rebates paid to buyers in a sale
options.c: Pay the rebate in cash after closing so it need not be disclosed to the lender
options.d: Follow brokerage rules on rebates and ensure any payment is lawful and disclosed

distractorExplanations.a: Earnest money is trust money for the transaction, not a source the licensee can use to pay a rebate.
distractorExplanations.b: RESPA does not ban disclosed rebates to buyers; legality turns on state law and lender disclosure.
distractorExplanations.c: Undisclosed rebates can be mortgage fraud; rebates must be disclosed to the lender and on the closing statement.

oh-real-estate-readiness-check-oh-licens.explanation: Rebate legality varies; compliance and disclosure are essential. The state commission's rules govern when rebates are permitted.

options.a: Perform licensed activities under the associate's license and supervision
options.b: Perform licensed activities only within their own license authority
options.c: Be paid commissions directly by the associate they work for
options.d: Negotiate offers for the associate's clients without broker affiliation

distractorExplanations.a: A licensee works under their own license and the broker's supervision, not another associate's license.
distractorExplanations.c: Compensation for licensed activity must flow through the employing broker, not directly from another associate.
distractorExplanations.d: Licensed activity requires affiliation with a broker; an unaffiliated license cannot be used to negotiate.

oh-real-estate-readiness-check-oh-licens.explanation: Licensed assistants still must stay within license and supervision rules. The assistant must also follow brokerage affiliation rules.

options.a: Protect confidential client information and not disclose without authority
options.b: Disclose it, since the duty of confidentiality ends when the transaction closes
options.c: Disclose it, because the buyer was a party to the same transaction
options.d: Refer the buyer to the cooperating agent, who may share it freely

distractorExplanations.b: Confidentiality can survive closing for non-public personal information; it does not end automatically at closing.
distractorExplanations.c: Being a party to the deal gives the buyer no right to the seller's personal contact information.
distractorExplanations.d: Passing the request to another agent does not make disclosure permissible; the information stays confidential.

oh-real-estate-readiness-check-oh-licens.explanation: Confidentiality can survive closing for non-public personal information. Disclosure is allowed only with authority or a legal requirement.

options.a: Licensed and holding an active E&O policy in their own name
options.b: Licensed and having finished the post-licensing course first
options.c: Licensed and operating their own office under a registered trade name
options.d: Properly licensed and affiliated with a supervising broker as required

distractorExplanations.a: E&O coverage is a risk tool, not the condition for practice; a salesperson must be affiliated with a broker.
distractorExplanations.b: Post-licensing education is due within the first year of licensure, not before a salesperson may practice.
distractorExplanations.c: Operating an independent office requires a broker license; a salesperson must work under a supervising broker.

options.a: Deposited into a properly designated trust/escrow account
options.b: Deposited into the brokerage's operating account until closing
options.c: Held by the listing agent in a personal account until closing
options.d: Given directly to the seller at signing

distractorExplanations.b: Placing trust money in the operating account is commingling; it must go into a designated trust account.
distractorExplanations.c: Trust funds belong in the broker's designated trust account, never a salesperson's personal account.
distractorExplanations.d: Earnest money is held in trust until closing or release, not paid to the seller when the contract is signed.

oh-real-estate-readiness-check-oh-licens.explanation: Timely deposit to a trust account is a core compliance duty. Deposits must be made within the required timelines.

options.a: Retake the state exam before joining the new brokerage
options.b: Follow transfer procedures so the license is properly affiliated
options.c: Apply for a new license number under the new brokerage
options.d: Wait until the next license renewal cycle to change their affiliation

distractorExplanations.a: Changing brokers is an affiliation transfer; there is no requirement to retake the licensing exam.
distractorExplanations.c: The license stays the same; only its affiliation transfers to the new broker.
distractorExplanations.d: Transfers are processed when the move happens; practicing for a new broker before transfer is not allowed.

oh-real-estate-readiness-check-oh-licens.explanation: Affiliation changes require regulatory notice/transfer steps. The licensee must notify the Ohio Division of Real Estate of the change.
